head: claude/decision-push-back
title: feat(work): push a committed decision answer back to the session that asked it
body:
## What this is

The last hop of the Phase H decision round-trip. Every hop is a push except the final one: the session that ASKED a decision question learns the answer only by polling. Operator, 2026-09-02:

> "Can we maybe add, like, a push something on the end of that so that, when the answer gets to the repo, it knows to push it to the session instead of waiting for the session to pull?"

**Draft. Not for merge — it carries an operator decision (see "What you need to decide").**

---

## STEP 1 — feasibility, established before any implementation

`docs/design/decision-push-back-FEASIBILITY.md`. Every claim is marked **TESTED** (a measurement made for the doc, with date and command), **READ** (documentation, explicitly *not* measured), or **RECORDED** (someone else's measurement, cited to where it lives). The dispatch expected a particular mechanism and the investigation found it does not work — so the answer is a different mechanism, not a shim.

**(a) Can an Actions runner fire a session-bound Routine? NO — and not on a single negative.**
The Routine `/fire` HTTP endpoint **does** exist, with a properly narrow per-routine bearer token. It is disqualified for two independent documented reasons: it **starts a NEW session** (`{"claude_code_session_id": "session_…"}` — a new id), and its token is minted **per-routine, from the web UI only** ("The CLI cannot currently create or revoke tokens"), so a design needing one routine per asking session needs a human click per question. Whether `/fire` would honour a `persistent_session_id` set via MCP is recorded as **UNKNOWN — undocumented and untested**, not asserted either way.

**(b) `watch_url`? NO — disqualified on a measurement, not an inference.**
TESTED this session: it returns a webhook URL plus a `sealed_secret` whose own result text says it "only works for this session and this webhook, and **only the artifact service can open it**". A GitHub runner is not the artifact service and cannot produce a delivery it would accept. That is fatal on its own; the watch also ends with the session, and — the security question the brief asked to treat as first-class — **a webhook URL committed to this PUBLIC repo is a published endpoint**, while a session cannot write an Actions secret, so there is nowhere safe to put it either. The webhook was stopped with `unwatch_url` immediately, and neither the URL nor the secret appears anywhere in this PR.

**(c) What actually works:** `claude -p "<msg>" --cloud <session-id>` — documented for exactly this ("send follow-ups from a CI script"), posts one message into an **existing** session and exits without waiting. Its documented error vocabulary is already the three states the brief demands.

---

## ⚠️ What you need to decide — this is why it is a draft

The delivery half is **built and unarmed**, because the credential is yours to originate and it is not free:

> "**There is no long-lived CI token for this today.** The scope that grants remote-session control, `user:sessions:claude_code`, is capped server-side at 30 days, so `claude setup-token` … doesn't cover it."

So `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` in Actions secrets **expires every 30 days and must be re-minted interactively**, and it is **account-wide session control** — far broader than "deliver one sentence to one session". Three options, and no code change is needed to take any of them:

1. **Mint it.** The channel arms itself; nothing else to do.
2. **Decline it.** The doc's §4.2 fallback is a two-hop design that needs **no new credential**: a scheduled fresh-session Routine holds `mcp__*` tools and can run the `create_trigger(persistent_session_id=…)` + `fire_trigger` sequence the manager measured working. Its missing hop is stated plainly rather than shimmed — nothing in the repo can *cause* that routine to exist; you create it once, and its minimum cadence is one hour.
3. **Do neither.** Everything still works exactly as it does today — see "Blast radius".

---

## STEP 2 — what is built

**The gating half: `asked_by` (this is the change that unblocks everything).**
Measured over the whole store: **ZERO decision requests carried any field naming the asking session**, so no committed answer had an address. `asked_by` records it; a session fills it from `get_session` with the id omitted (TESTED: returns its own record). Three states, never collapsed, registered with `collapsed-state-guard`: `recorded` / `unrecorded` (blameless — every pre-existing request, and any question a human asked) / `malformed` (an asker WAS recorded and is unusable — a question whose answer will *silently never be delivered* while its owner believes it will; a finding that fails the run).

⚠️ **Existing requests are deliberately NOT back-filled.** Inventing an asker for `DEC-20260901-READ-GATE-SEQUENCING` would assert a fact nobody established. `unrecorded` exists precisely so that gap is not papered over — so the field ships live with a population of zero.

**The delivery decision, as a pure function** (`src/runtime/decision_push.py`), so the policy that declares a session dead is arguable in tests rather than against a live session — the discipline this repo adopted after an automated remediation cancelled the leg that matched the journal.

| state | when |
|---|---|
| `pushed` | the delivery command's own `ok: true` — nothing else |
| `session_gone` | **only** the platform's two documented "cannot receive" signals. A **real state, not an error** |
| `unknown` | **everything else**, and the default: no credential, a timeout, a 529, an `ok:false` we cannot attribute, exit 0 with nothing parsable |

⚠️ **The pair that matters is `session_gone` vs `unknown`.** A `session_gone` verdict writes a marker, and the marker stops all future attempts — so grading a network blip as `session_gone` would **permanently strand an answer for a session that was alive the whole time**. `unknown` therefore writes **nothing** and is retried. Also recorded: an **expired** session is *not* gone (its history is restored on reopen), and whether a queued message survives that is UNKNOWN — which is exactly why the unrecognised case is `unknown`.

**Idempotence comes from the repo**, never from the workflow remembering — a `push:` block on the committed answer. ⚠️ The residual is stated rather than hidden: if a delivery succeeds and the marker then fails to land, the next run pushes again. That direction is chosen — a duplicate wake tells the session the same true thing twice, whereas writing the marker *before* delivering would make a **failed** delivery read as pushed.

**The message CARRIES the answer**, quoted in full — because a woken turn may have no `mcp__*` tools, so "go read the PR" would strand it — and says on its face that it is one-way and nobody is waiting for a reply.

---

## Blast radius

**This ADDS push; it does not replace pull.** `/api/bot/work/decisions` still grades `committed` from the repo exactly as before. **If every delivery failed forever, the system would behave exactly as it does today.** That is what makes `session_gone` survivable rather than a lost answer.

With the secret unset the two new steps are **skipped**, and the script prints `channel: off_no_credential` rather than looking green. No order path, no config, no VM state; the only new outbound call is one CLI command that exists only when the operator arms it.

---

## Verification — stated honestly

- `tests/test_decision_push.py` — **45 passing**, including the adversarial cases: 8 distinct failure shapes must all grade `unknown`; a missing credential must not grade `session_gone`; "archived" in unrelated prose must not trip the gone-pattern; the writer cannot produce a block its own reader calls `malformed`.
- **Measured end to end** over a real objects directory: credential off → 0 delivery calls, 0 markers; armed → `pushed`/`session_gone` written, `unknown` **not** written; re-run → only the `unknown` retried, 1 call instead of 3.
- Repo guards: **53 PASS / 0 FAIL**. `collapsed-state-guard` clean at 30 contracts with the two new ones registered and branched on by real consumers.

⚠️ **WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, and no green tick here changes it:** **no answer has ever been pushed to a real session.** A green suite proves the decision function; a green workflow run with the secret unset is the *expected output of a channel that is switched off*. Tracked as a loud `OPEN-ITEMS` row that clears only on an **observed wake** — the asking session read idle before and running after, doing something attributable — and explicitly **not** on a merge, a green run, or a passing test. If you decline the credential, that row **changes rather than clears**: push-back over the CLI becomes a *recorded decision*, not a channel that looks like it is about to work.

⚠️ `tests/test_work_decisions.py` could not be run here — it fails at import with a `pyo3` panic in the pydantic stack, **confirmed identical at `origin/main`** by stashing this change. Environmental, not from this PR, but it means CI is the first place the existing suite actually runs against it.

---

## Coordination

▶️ START posted to #6927 ([comment](https://github.com/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/issues/6927#issuecomment-5508300445)) via the `board-post` relay — `add_issue_comment` 403s from this session while `issue_read` on the same issue succeeds, so this is the documented write-scope boundary, not the transient MCP drop. No overlap with MI-57 (`open_pr_record.py`, `handoff_check.py`) or MI-58/59 (`telegram_query_bot.py`); the one shared file, `work_decisions.py`, is touched **additively only**.
